ev.q: Mask mandates were associated with a 0.5 percentage point decrease (p = 0.02) in daily COVID-19 case growth rates 1–20 days after implementation
Allowing on-premises dining at restaurants was associated with 2.2 and 3.0 percentage point increases in the death growth rate 61–80 and 81–100 days
the daily percentage point growth rate of county-level COVID-19 cases and county-level COVID-19 deaths
state-issued mask mandates applied in 2,313 (73.6%) of the 3,142 U.S. counties
Daily case and death growth rates before implementation of mask mandates were not statistically different from the reference period.
The regression models controlled for several covariates
Associations between the policies and COVID-19 outcomes were measured using a reference period (1–20 days before implementation)
all analyses were conducted at the county level
Mask mandates were associated with statistically significant decreases in county-level daily COVID-19 case and death growth rates

methods_quotes.q: Weighted least-squares regression with county and day fixed effects was used to compare COVID-19 case and death growth rates before and after
All analyses were weighted by county population with standard errors robust to heteroscedasticity and clustered by state.
The daily growth rate was defined as the difference between the natural log of cumulative cases or deaths on a given day
Associations between the policies and COVID-19 outcomes were measured using a reference period (1–20 days before implementation)
The regression models controlled for several covariates: restaurant closures in the mask mandate models and mask mandates in the restaurant reopening models
